A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of Rodrigues Network for Learning Robot Actions. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching v1 Appendices B–E to v2 Appendices C–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original forward-kinematics fitting, motion prediction, simulated imitation-learning, and hand-reconstruction results, with additional ablations, sensitivity studies, and runtime measurements in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the work's original experiments and results in Section 5 and the appendices, including benchmark evaluations, ablations, sensitivity studies, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The learned operator, Rodrigues Block, quaternion adaptation, and task-specific architectures remain unchanged. Section 4 and new Appendix B clarify feature propagation and input/output interfaces without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use LEAP Hand forward kinematics, UR5 motion prediction, the same five ManiSkill manipulation tasks, and single-image hand reconstruction evaluated on FreiHAND. The hand-training datasets and test scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The synthetic experiments retain MLP, GCN, BoT, and Transformer comparators. Table 2 retains Transformer-DP and UNet-DP, and Table 3 retains the same hand-reconstruction comparators, including published and reproduced HaMeR.

E3.justification: Matched experimental appendices retain data generation, splits, metrics, training budgets, hyperparameters, model sizes, and evaluation procedures. New Appendix B supplies architectural documentation rather than revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: The component ablations, baseline-size comparisons, and channel/depth sensitivity studies are retained in v2 Appendix E from v1 Appendix D. Tables 11–12, Figure 6, and the existing qualitative examples test the same questions with unchanged evidence.

E5.justification: The uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged, including five-seed means and standard deviations for imitation learning. Table 1 changes numerical uncertainty values, but neither version documents a corresponding change in runs or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1's ErrorT uncertainty values change from ±0.05, ±0.05, ±0.04, ±0.06, and ±0.04 to ±0.33, ±0.44, ±0.29, ±0.45, and ±0.17 for MLP, GCN, BoT, Transformer, and Rodrigues, respectively. All means and rankings remain unchanged. Figure 4's explicit MLP-versus-GCN position/orientation comparison is also removed from its caption.

T1.justification: Equation 3 corrects Rodrigues' rotation formula by restoring the square on the skew-symmetric matrix in the (1 − cos θ) term. This fixes a mathematical error; the subsequent learned-operator derivation and quaternion equations are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its framing from enforcing structural constraints to exploiting kinematic computational patterns as an inductive bias. It also omits its imitation-learning state-of-the-art assertion, although Section 5.2 retains that assertion. The abstract and conclusion preserve the central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 changes tactile or force feedback from something contact tasks likely require to something beneficial, explicitly noting its absence from the environment. The limitations concerning link geometry, translational joints, and untested reinforcement-learning applicability remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix B consolidates input embeddings and output-head descriptions and newly specifies learnable initial embeddings for hand reconstruction. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, runtime information, CUDA implementation details, and promises to release code, data, and checkpoints are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Harris et al.'s corner-detector reference and replaces the AlexNet citation with LeCun et al.'s document-recognition work. It removes several background references, including Decision Transformer and JoLo-GCN. The central positioning against graph connectivity, masked attention, and analytical kinematics remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Selected introductory and limitations paragraphs are rewritten, layer behavior is explained more explicitly, and appendix cross-references become more precise. Appendix B is inserted and subsequent appendices renumbered. Affiliations and acknowledgements are updated, while most technical and experimental prose remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts ICLR formatting, revises Figure 2's architecture diagram, relocates existing displays, and adjusts table formatting and captions. Figure 4's caption is shortened and Table 2 explicitly identifies simulated success rates. The same six figures and twelve tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes the incorrect rotation formula in Equation 3 and improves architectural clarity through revised Figure 2, explicit feature-flow explanations, and Appendix B's implementation details. These provide limited gains in correctness and reproducibility. Experimental coverage and central performance evidence remain essentially unchanged; the revised Table 1 uncertainties do not establish a performance improvement.
